pieces.label: 第一人称手臂＋武器组合

sources.author: Quaternius (rifle geometry), original hands/arms/sleeves recipe in this repository
sources.identity: Derived, not the source OBJ: RX-24 parts already normalized to camera-local -Z and split into 24 named parts.

sources.author: Quaternius
sources.identity: Original editable source mesh; build.mjs does not re-export it, it consumes the reviewed derived JSON.

derivation: Merge the 24 reviewed rifle parts into static receiver and magazine nodes; the charging handle is an original bevelled box node, not source geometry. Keep source part colours as linear vertex colours.
Rebuild the original palm/finger/wrist/sleeve recipe from src/render/rifle.ts at the rest pose and attach it to support-hand and trigger-hand nodes.
Reorient every source triangle outward against its part centre; bake flat normals and 8-sided tube facets.
Re-anchor node origins at magazine, bolt, support palm and trigger palm so runtime reload can translate those nodes without touching the static receiver.

actions.name: idle
actions.notes: Feet and aim are owned by the player controller; the view model only breathes.

actions.name: move
actions.notes: src/render/weapon.ts sways at 9 rad/s by 4 mm and widens the crosshair; no baked move clip, because sway must track current speed.

actions.name: fire
actions.notes: Root kick is presentation only. Ray direction and recoil remain src/sim values and are not changed by this clip.

actions.name: reload
actions.notes: The whole-gun lowering and the support-hand path stay procedural in src/render/weapon.ts and src/render/arm.ts. The GLB supplies the magazine and bolt nodes so a future segmented view model can play the same phases; do not replace the reload with a single rifle tilt.

actions.name: hit
actions.notes: First-person arms do not receive the enemy hit reaction; the hit-feedback piece owns hit confirmation.

actions.name: death
actions.notes: The player view is hidden on death by src/render/scene.ts; no death clip is exported.

clips.name: idle
clips.source: original recipe; breathing sway, no ballistic effect

clips.name: fire
clips.source: src/render/weapon.ts weaponPose kick envelope, sampled at 20 ms

clips.name: reload-magazine
clips.source: WEAPONS.rifle.reload = 114 ticks at 60 Hz; withdraw 0.22-0.55, insert 0.55-0.77

clips.name: reload-bolt
clips.source: bolt-close phase 0.77-0.89 of the same reload clock

gaps: No skinned hand rig: the support hand and sleeve remain a rest-pose recipe, so runtime keeps rebuilding the sleeve from two arm segments.
The GLB is not loaded by src. Wiring needs a GLTFLoader path plus per-node pose application that preserves the existing simulation clock.
Finger contact and screen coverage in idle, fire and reload must be judged in the real game view; geometry checks are only regression gates.
pieces.status: Visual, palette and budget standard. Runtime keeps its procedural view-model for now; GLB is not wired into src.

pieces.label: 敌方全身角色

sources.author: Casti_131, Low Poly Soldier with weapons
sources.identity: Derived posed mesh, 309 vertices / 515 triangles, metres, feet at y=0; source ZIP and Blend hashes are recorded in assets/characters/relay-guard/README.md.

derivation: Split the posed mesh into head, spine, left leg, right leg and weapon rigid groups with pivots at head base, waist, hips and rifle grip.
Recolour helmet, carrier and cloth as the enemy warm family using the existing targetColor recipe; keep the visor, belt and weapon source values.
Bake per-face vertex colours, flat normals and the runtime axis flip (x, y, -z) used by src/render/scene.ts.
Author five rigid-group clips (idle, walk, fire, hit, death) as glTF node TRS animation; no skin is claimed.

actions.name: fire
actions.notes: Presentation only; bot accuracy and fire cadence stay in src/sim/bot.ts.

actions.name: reload
actions.notes: Bots emit reload at src/sim/bot.ts:66 and :75. The enemy mesh has no separate magazine node, so no reload clip is claimed; adding one requires splitting the weapon mesh first.

actions.name: crouch
actions.notes: src/render/target.ts squashes height to 0.65; the exported mesh keeps the standing pose.

clips.name: walk
clips.source: original two-step loop; hip swing 0.38 rad forward / 0.30 rad back

clips.name: fire
clips.source: original 120 ms reaction performance; the runtime muzzle flash is 65 ms in src/render/weapon.ts, not this clip's length

clips.name: death
clips.source: src/render/feedback.ts fall ramp to 0.47 pi in 600 ms

gaps: Rigid groups are not a skin: elbows, knees and the rifle grip do not deform, and the arms keep the source aiming pose.
Walk and death are node-level approximations; foot contact and silhouette need the real game view with the courtyard lighting.
The source weapon geometry is inside the body mesh; a real reload needs the rifle and magazine split into their own nodes.
No in-game GPU roster or side-by-side comparison exists yet; this file does not claim final quality.
pieces.status: Full-body standard with rigid action groups. Gait and arm poses are approximations; in-game comparison is not done.

pieces.label: 可读的通路／掩体建筑

sources.author: Rob Tuytel / Poly Haven
sources.identity: Unchanged 1K colour source. This piece reuses the already adopted 2 m courtyard texture slot; it does not embed or re-derive the image.

derivation: Original procedural assembly: 12 m corridor, 3.0 m walls, two 1.2 m x 2.2 m doorways at z=0 and z=4, one half-wall and one crate cover.
Object-space UVs are metres / 2 so the existing courtyard concrete slot tiles without a new texture.

Dimensions, module instances and collision boxes are recorded in the GLB scene extras (three.js gltf.scene.userData), the same source as contracts/passage-cover.actions.json; they do not change src/content/map.ts.

actions.name: static
actions.notes: The standard is static architecture; it owns no door, hinge or destruction animation.

actions.name: door
actions.notes: Each doorway is an open pass-through, not a moving door.

gaps: The assembly is not placed in src/content/map.ts; the collision boxes here are design data until the case line wires them.
Visible join covers and corner trims are geometric, but no normal/AO map is added; the existing lighting still has to prove readability.
The corridor is one assembled reference. A modular runtime kit would need each wall cut into its own node; this piece does not claim modular streaming.
pieces.status: Readable assembled passage, not yet placed into src/content/map.ts or src/render/scene.ts.

pieces.label: 命中反馈标准件

sources.author: Original repository recipe
sources.identity: Marker geometry, burst, colour roles and timeline are original. Timing is cross-checked against src/render/feedback.ts, but no source art or code file is copied into the artifact.

derivation: Original four-tick marker with a headshot ring and a separate low-poly impact burst; no copied HUD art.
Marker units are metres at a 0.5 m billboard plane; runtime may also scale it in pixels.
Colour roles: body white, head signal, kill signal-hot, friendly faction-cool; impact spark warm.

actions.name: hit-body
actions.sound: existing synth 'hit' cue, no new recording

actions.name: hit-head
actions.colorRole: signal amber ring plus white ticks

actions.name: hit-kill
actions.colorRole: signal-hot ticks plus amber ring, 700 ms hold

actions.name: friendly
actions.notes: src/ui/hud.ts already distinguishes friendly hits by dataset kind; do not show a kill accent for friendlies.

actions.name: miss
actions.notes: A miss must not create a hit marker or a hit sound.

actions.name: impact
actions.colorRole: impact spark warm; actor hits use a smaller 1.2x burst, world hits 1.8x
actions.notes: src/render/scene.ts currently uses a 0.035 m sphere; this piece replaces it with a faceted burst.

clips.name: hit-body
clips.source: src/ui/hud.ts shows the body marker for 320 ms; this clip owns the 120 ms pop

clips.name: hit-head
clips.source: src/render/feedback.ts flinch is 180 ms; the head marker matches it

clips.name: impact
clips.source: src/render/scene.ts hides impact spheres after 180 ms

gaps: The GLB is not loaded by src; the current CSS marker and impact sphere remain until the case line wires them.
No new sound is authored: the existing synth hit/head/kill cues are the sound role contract, and audio-visual frame sync is not measured.
The friendly state is a colour contract, not a separately exported mesh.
The 14 px screen size is a target; it is not measured on a real GPU window yet.
pieces.status: Geometry and timeline standard. Current runtime still uses the CSS hit marker and impact sphere; not wired.
